name: ESDSRRDS.jcl
description:
This JCL job initializes and loads user security data for the CardDemo application by creating two VSAM files — an Entry Sequenced Dataset (ESDS) and a Relative Record Dataset (RRDS) — and populating both with 10 user records (5 administrators and 5 regular users), each containing user ID, first name, last name, and password information in an 80-byte fixed format.Key Functionalities:
Creates a temporary sequential flat file containing 10 user security records: 5 administrator accounts (ADMIN001–ADMIN005) and 5 regular user accounts (USER0001–USER0005), each with first name, last name, and an associated password.
Deletes any pre-existing VSAM ESDS cluster (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.USRSEC.VSAM.ESDS) and redefines it as a new Non-Indexed (Entry Sequenced) VSAM cluster with 80-byte fixed records, allocated at 45 primary and 15 secondary tracks, then loads all 10 user records into it.
Deletes any pre-existing VSAM RRDS cluster (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.USRSEC.VSAM.RRDS) and redefines it as a new Numbered (Relative Record) VSAM cluster with 80-byte fixed records, allocated at 45 primary and 15 secondary tracks, then loads all 10 user records into it.
Ensures a clean initialization by first removing any prior version of the temporary sequential file before recreating it, preventing stale or duplicate data from being loaded into the VSAM files.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The CardDemo User Security initialization job is about to begin, and the User Security staging file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.ESDSRRDS.PS) may or may not exist from a previous run
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The pre-deletion step executes at the start of the initialization job
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The User Security staging file must be deleted under ALL of the following conditions: (1) If the file exists and the step completes successfully — the file is deleted; (2) If the file exists and the step encounters an error — the file is still deleted; (3) If the file does not exist — no error is raised and the step completes silently, allowing the job to continue; ensuring that in every scenario, no residual staging data from any prior execution remains before the new initialization begins

rules.Rule_Name: PREDEL - IEFBR14 - Unconditional Deletion of User Security Staging File Before Initialization
rules.Rule_Description: Before the CardDemo User Security initialization process begins, the staging file used to seed user security data must be completely removed — regardless of whether it exists, and regardless of whether the deletion step itself succeeds or fails — to ensure no stale data from a prior run can contaminate the current initialization.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The CardDemo User Security initialization job is being executed to establish the initial set of user accounts
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the user security seed data for loading
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Exactly 10 user security records must be defined: 5 Administrator accounts (ADMIN001 through ADMIN005) and 5 Standard User accounts (USER0001 through USER0005), each record being exactly 80 characters in fixed-length format containing User ID, First Name, Last Name, and Password fields

rules.Rule_Name: STEP01 - IEBGENER - Define Initial User Security Seed Records
rules.Rule_Description: The CardDemo application requires a fixed set of 10 initial user security accounts — 5 Administrators and 5 Standard Users — to be defined as seed data for the User Security data stores. Each account must carry a User ID, First Name, Last Name, and Password within a fixed 80-character record structure.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user security record is being created for the CardDemo User Security data store
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The record is written to the staging file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The record must be exactly 80 characters long with the following fixed-position layout: User ID in positions 1–8 (8 characters), First Name in positions 9–28 (20 characters, space-padded), Last Name in positions 29–48 (20 characters, space-padded), Password in positions 49–57 (9 characters), and remaining positions 58–80 left as trailing spaces

rules.Rule_Name: STEP01 - IEBGENER - User Security Record Layout Definition
rules.Rule_Description: Every user security record in the CardDemo application must conform to a fixed 80-character layout with four defined fields occupying specific positions. This structure is mandatory for all user accounts regardless of account type.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user security record is being defined as an Administrator account in the CardDemo application
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The record is written to the User Security staging file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The User ID field (positions 1–8) must begin with the prefix 'ADMIN' followed by a 3-digit sequential number (ADMIN001, ADMIN002, ADMIN003, ADMIN004, ADMIN005), AND the Password field must be set to 'PASSWORDA' — where the suffix 'A' designates Administrator-level access

rules.Rule_Name: STEP01 - IEBGENER - Administrator Account Identification Rule
rules.Rule_Description: Administrator accounts in CardDemo are distinguished from Standard User accounts by specific patterns in both the User ID and the Password fields. These patterns must be consistently applied across all Administrator seed records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user security record is being defined as a Standard User account in the CardDemo application
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The record is written to the User Security staging file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The User ID field (positions 1–8) must begin with the prefix 'USER' followed by a 4-digit sequential number (USER0001, USER0002, USER0003, USER0004, USER0005), AND the Password field must be set to 'PASSWORDU' — where the suffix 'U' designates Standard User-level access

rules.Rule_Name: STEP01 - IEBGENER - Standard User Account Identification Rule
rules.Rule_Description: Standard User accounts in CardDemo are distinguished from Administrator accounts by specific patterns in both the User ID and the Password fields. These patterns must be consistently applied across all Standard User seed records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The CardDemo User Security initialization job is preparing Administrator seed accounts
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The 5 Administrator records are written to the User Security staging file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The following 5 Administrator records must be created exactly as specified: (1) ADMIN001 — First Name: MARGARET, Last Name: GOLD, Password: PASSWORDA; (2) ADMIN002 — First Name: RUSSELL, Last Name: RUSSELL, Password: PASSWORDA; (3) ADMIN003 — First Name: RAYMOND, Last Name: WHITMORE, Password: PASSWORDA; (4) ADMIN004 — First Name: EMMANUEL, Last Name: CASGRAIN, Password: PASSWORDA; (5) ADMIN005 — First Name: GRANVILLE, Last Name: LACHAPELLE, Password: PASSWORDA

rules.Rule_Name: STEP01 - IEBGENER - Seed Administrator Account Records
rules.Rule_Description: The CardDemo application must be initialized with exactly 5 Administrator accounts with predefined identities. These accounts represent the initial administrative users of the system and their details are fixed at initialization time.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The CardDemo User Security initialization job is preparing Standard User seed accounts
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The 5 Standard User records are written to the User Security staging file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The following 5 Standard User records must be created exactly as specified: (1) USER0001 — First Name: LAWRENCE, Last Name: THOMAS, Password: PASSWORDU; (2) USER0002 — First Name: AJITH, Last Name: KUMAR, Password: PASSWORDU; (3) USER0003 — First Name: LAURITZ, Last Name: ALME, Password: PASSWORDU; (4) USER0004 — First Name: AVERARDO, Last Name: MAZZI, Password: PASSWORDU; (5) USER0005 — First Name: LEE, Last Name: TING, Password: PASSWORDU

rules.Rule_Name: STEP01 - IEBGENER - Seed Standard User Account Records
rules.Rule_Description: The CardDemo application must be initialized with exactly 5 Standard User accounts with predefined identities. These accounts represent the initial standard users of the system and their details are fixed at initialization time.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The CardDemo User Security staging file is being populated with the 10 seed records
Acceptance_Criteria.When: All 10 records are written to the staging file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Records must be written in the following strict order: first the 5 Administrator records in sequence (ADMIN001, ADMIN002, ADMIN003, ADMIN004, ADMIN005), followed by the 5 Standard User records in sequence (USER0001, USER0002, USER0003, USER0004, USER0005) — resulting in Administrators occupying positions 1–5 and Standard Users occupying positions 6–10

rules.Rule_Name: STEP01 - IEBGENER - Record Ordering Rule for User Security Staging File
rules.Rule_Description: The order in which user security records are written to the staging file determines their slot positions in the RRDS and their sequential positions in the ESDS. Administrator records must precede Standard User records to ensure consistent positional assignment.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The CardDemo User Security initialization job is writing the 10 seed records to the staging file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The staging file creation completes — either successfully or with a failure
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the file is created successfully, it must be catalogued and retained for use in the downstream ESDS and RRDS loading steps; AND if the file creation fails for any reason, the incomplete staging file must be automatically deleted to prevent corrupt or partial data from being carried forward to the VSAM loading steps

rules.Rule_Name: STEP01 - IEBGENER - User Security Staging File Creation and Integrity Rule
rules.Rule_Description: The User Security staging file must be created as a new, catalogued file to serve as the single source of truth for seeding both VSAM data stores. If the file creation fails for any reason, the incomplete file must be automatically discarded to prevent partial or corrupt data from being used in downstream loading steps.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The 10 hardcoded user security seed records are being written to the User Security staging file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The copy operation is performed by the system
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All 10 records must be written to the staging file exactly as defined in the source data — with no field modifications, no record filtering, no data reformatting, and no record reordering — ensuring the staging file is an exact replica of the seed data

rules.Rule_Name: STEP01 - IEBGENER - No Transformation Policy for Seed Data
rules.Rule_Description: The user security seed records must be copied to the staging file exactly as defined — without any modification, filtering, reformatting, or transformation. The data must reach the VSAM data stores in its original form.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Security ESDS (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.USRSEC.VSAM.ESDS) may or may not exist in the system catalog
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User Security initialization job is executed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The existing User Security ESDS (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.USRSEC.VSAM.ESDS) and its data component (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.USRSEC.VSAM.ESDS.DAT) must be deleted from the system catalog before any new data is loaded

rules.Rule_Name: STEP02 - IDCAMS - Delete Existing User Security ESDS Before Reinitialization
rules.Rule_Description: Before recreating the User Security Entry-Sequenced Dataset (ESDS), any previously existing version must be removed to ensure the initialization always starts with a clean, empty data store.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The DELETE operation for the User Security ESDS (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.USRSEC.VSAM.ESDS) has been attempted
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The DELETE operation raises an error because the User Security ESDS does not exist in the system catalog (first-time run or file was previously removed)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error condition must be reset to zero (MAXCC = 0) so that the subsequent User Security ESDS creation step is not blocked, and the initialization process continues successfully without requiring manual intervention

rules.Rule_Name: STEP02 - IDCAMS - Suppress Deletion Failure for First-Time User Security ESDS Initialization
rules.Rule_Description: The initialization process must be run-safe — it must succeed regardless of whether the User Security ESDS already exists or is being created for the very first time. If the deletion fails because the file does not exist, the failure must be suppressed so that the creation step can proceed without interruption.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The existing User Security ESDS has been deleted (or confirmed as non-existent) and the error condition has been reset to zero
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User Security ESDS creation is executed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A new User Security ESDS cluster named AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.USRSEC.VSAM.ESDS must be created with ALL of the following properties: (1) Each user security record must be exactly 80 characters in both minimum and maximum length (RECORDSIZE 80,80); (2) The dataset must be Entry-Sequenced (NONINDEXED) so that records are stored and retrieved in the exact order they are written, supporting sequential batch processing of all user accounts; (3) The dataset must be flagged as reusable (REUSE) so it can be reloaded with fresh data in future initialization runs without requiring deletion and recreation; (4) Storage must be allocated with 45 primary tracks and 15 secondary tracks (TRACKS 45,15) to accommodate the initial 10 user records and future growth; (5) Free space must be reserved at 10% per Control Interval and 15% per Control Area (FREESPACE 10,15) to allow for future record insertions without reorganization; (6) The Control Interval size must be set to 8192 bytes (CISZ 8192) for optimal read/write performance; (7) The physical data component must be named AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.USRSEC.VSAM.ESDS.DAT

rules.Rule_Name: STEP02 - IDCAMS - Define User Security ESDS with Fixed Record Structure and Sequential Access
rules.Rule_Description: A new User Security Entry-Sequenced Dataset (ESDS) must be created with a precisely defined structure that supports fixed-length 80-character user security records and sequential batch processing. The dataset must be reusable across multiple initialization runs.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Security staging file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.ESDSRRDS.PS) exists and contains all 10 user security records (5 Administrator accounts and 5 Standard User accounts), AND the User Security ESDS (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.USRSEC.VSAM.ESDS) has been freshly created and is empty
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system copies all records from the User Security staging file into the User Security ESDS without any modification, filtering, or transformation, preserving the exact order and content of every record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All 10 user security records are loaded into the User Security ESDS in the same sequential order as they appear in the staging file — 5 Administrator accounts (ADMIN001–ADMIN005) followed by 5 Standard User accounts (USER0001–USER0005) — and the User Security ESDS is fully populated and ready for sequential batch access by the CardDemo application

rules.Rule_Name: STEP03 - IDCAMS REPRO - Load All User Security Records into User Security ESDS
rules.Rule_Description: All user security records from the staging sequential file are copied as-is into the User Security Entry-Sequenced Dataset (ESDS), making them available for sequential batch processing by the CardDemo application.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The CardDemo User Security RRDS dataset (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.USRSEC.VSAM.RRDS) may or may not exist in the system catalog from a prior initialization run
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User Security data layer initialization process is triggered
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must attempt to delete the existing User Security RRDS dataset (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.USRSEC.VSAM.RRDS) along with its data component (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.USRSEC.VSAM.RRDS.DAT) to clear all previously loaded user security records before reinitialization begins

rules.Rule_Name: STEP04 - IDCAMS - Delete Existing User Security RRDS Before Reinitialization
rules.Rule_Description: Before creating a fresh User Security Relative Record Dataset (RRDS), any previously existing version of the dataset must be removed to ensure no stale or duplicate user security data persists across initialization runs.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The deletion of the User Security RRDS (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.USRSEC.VSAM.RRDS) has been attempted AND the dataset did not exist, causing the delete operation to raise a non-zero error condition
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The error condition from the failed delete is evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error condition must be reset to zero (MAXCC = 0) so that the subsequent User Security RRDS creation step is not blocked, allowing the initialization to proceed successfully on both first-time runs and re-runs

rules.Rule_Name: STEP04 - IDCAMS - Suppress Delete Failure to Ensure First-Time Run Safety
rules.Rule_Description: The initialization process must succeed even when the User Security RRDS does not yet exist in the system — such as during the very first execution. Any error raised by the delete attempt must be suppressed so that the dataset creation step is not blocked.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The existing User Security RRDS has been deleted (or confirmed not to exist) AND the error condition has been reset to zero
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User Security RRDS creation is executed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A new VSAM Relative Record Dataset named AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.USRSEC.VSAM.RRDS must be created with the following business specifications: (1) Dataset organized as NUMBERED (Relative Record) to support direct positional access to individual user security records by slot number; (2) Each user security record must be exactly 80 characters in both minimum and maximum length to match the fixed-length user security record structure; (3) The dataset must be REUSE-enabled so it can be reloaded with refreshed user security data without requiring deletion and recreation; (4) A data component named AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.USRSEC.VSAM.RRDS.DAT must be created to physically store the user security records

rules.Rule_Name: STEP04 - IDCAMS - Define User Security RRDS for Direct Positional Access
rules.Rule_Description: A new User Security Relative Record Dataset (RRDS) must be created as the primary data store for online user authentication in the CardDemo application. The RRDS enables the application to retrieve any individual user's security record instantly by its assigned slot number, without scanning through all records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Security RRDS (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.USRSEC.VSAM.RRDS) is being defined for the CardDemo application
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The storage parameters are applied during dataset creation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The dataset must be allocated with: (1) A primary storage allocation of 45 tracks to hold the initial user security records with room for growth; (2) A secondary storage allocation of 15 tracks to automatically extend storage if the primary allocation is exhausted; (3) A free space reservation of 10% within each Control Interval and 15% within each Control Area to allow efficient insertion of new user security records without immediate reorganization; (4) A Control Interval size of 8192 bytes (8KB) to optimize read and write performance for user security record access

rules.Rule_Name: STEP04 - IDCAMS - Allocate Sufficient Storage for User Security RRDS
rules.Rule_Description: The User Security RRDS must be allocated with sufficient storage capacity to hold the initial set of user security records and accommodate future growth, while reserving free space to allow efficient record insertion and updates without reorganization.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Security staging file (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.ESDSRRDS.PS) exists and contains 10 user security records — 5 Administrator accounts (ADMIN001–ADMIN005) followed by 5 Standard User accounts (USER0001–USER0005) — and the User Security RRDS (AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.USRSEC.VSAM.RRDS) has been freshly created and is empty
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The REPRO operation is executed to copy all records from the staging file into the User Security RRDS
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All 10 user security records must be written into the User Security RRDS without any modification to their content, each record occupying a fixed sequential slot number determined by its position in the staging file — Administrator accounts are assigned slots 1 through 5 and Standard User accounts are assigned slots 6 through 10 — so that any individual user security record can be retrieved directly by its slot number during online CardDemo application use

rules.Rule_Name: STEP05 - IDCAMS REPRO - Load All User Security Records into RRDS
rules.Rule_Description: All user security records from the staging sequential file are copied as-is into the User Security Relative Record Dataset (RRDS), assigning each record a sequential slot number based on its position in the input file. This enables the CardDemo application to perform direct positional access to individual user security records during online authentication.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Security staging file contains fixed 80-character records, each holding a User ID, First Name, Last Name, and Password for a CardDemo user account
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The REPRO operation copies each record from the staging file to the User Security RRDS
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Every record written to the User Security RRDS must be identical in content to its corresponding record in the staging file — no fields may be modified, truncated, padded differently, or reordered — and the total record count in the RRDS must exactly match the total record count in the staging file

rules.Rule_Name: STEP05 - IDCAMS REPRO - Preserve User Security Record Integrity During Load
rules.Rule_Description: Each user security record copied from the staging file into the RRDS must retain its exact original content — User ID, First Name, Last Name, and Password — without any alteration, ensuring the RRDS is a faithful replica of the seed data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Security staging file contains 10 records in a defined order — ADMIN001 (MARGARET GOLD) first, followed by ADMIN002 (RUSSELL RUSSELL), ADMIN003 (RAYMOND WHITMORE), ADMIN004 (EMMANUEL CASGRAIN), ADMIN005 (GRANVILLE LACHAPELLE), USER0001 (LAWRENCE THOMAS), USER0002 (AJITH KUMAR), USER0003 (LAURITZ ALME), USER0004 (AVERARDO MAZZI), and USER0005 (LEE TING) last — and the User Security RRDS is empty and ready to receive records
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The REPRO operation loads all records sequentially from the staging file into the User Security RRDS
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Each user security record must be assigned a slot number that corresponds to its position in the staging file: ADMIN001 receives slot 1, ADMIN002 receives slot 2, ADMIN003 receives slot 3, ADMIN004 receives slot 4, ADMIN005 receives slot 5, USER0001 receives slot 6, USER0002 receives slot 7, USER0003 receives slot 8, USER0004 receives slot 9, and USER0005 receives slot 10 — ensuring that the CardDemo application can directly retrieve any user's security record by referencing its assigned slot number

rules.Rule_Name: STEP05 - IDCAMS REPRO - Assign Sequential Slot Numbers to User Security Records in RRDS
rules.Rule_Description: The RRDS assigns a fixed positional slot number to each user security record based on the order in which it is loaded from the staging file. This slot number becomes the permanent direct-access key for that user's security record in the CardDemo application.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Security RRDS has been successfully populated with all 10 user security records, each assigned a unique sequential slot number (1 through 10)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The CardDemo application needs to authenticate or retrieve the security details of a specific user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The CardDemo application must be able to access that user's security record — containing their User ID, First Name, Last Name, and Password — directly by their assigned slot number without reading any other records in the RRDS, enabling fast and efficient online user authentication

rules.Rule_Name: STEP05 - IDCAMS REPRO - Enable Direct Positional Access for Online User Authentication
rules.Rule_Description: By loading user security records into the RRDS, the CardDemo application gains the ability to authenticate any individual user instantly by accessing their record directly via slot number, without scanning through all other user records.
